# `folder_workload` — version 2.1

Source: `presets/folder-workload.satz`

## Purpose

Delegated access to folders: one identity per workload, and the folders it works in.
The account holds its roles on those folders alone. A workload is a team's or a product's
set of deployments — a shop, a RAG store per customer — that is rolled out by an estate of
its own beside this one. The pack gives it an infrastructure project with the service
account its pipelines run as and the bucket its states live in, creates the folders it may
work in, and grants the account its roles on THOSE folders and nowhere else.

TWO LISTS. One entry of `folder_workloads` is one identity:
{ name = "shop" group = "gcp-shop-admins@example.com" }
One entry of `folder_workload_folders` is one folder the pack creates, and the workload
whose account works in it:
{ name = "shop-frontend" workload = "shop" }
{ name = "shop-data"     workload = "shop" parent = "google_folder.data.name" }
A workload works in as many folders as name it, and they need no common root: `parent` is
`google_folder.workload_folder.name` unless the entry names another folder the estate
declares (`google_folder.<label>.name`) or one that already exists (`folders/<id>`). Both
lists are bound in the estate or requested by the team as `contributes_folder_workloads` /
`contributes_folder_workload_folders` in a small pack of its own, checked with
`satz check-request` and vendored by pull request. A `name` is lowercase letters, digits
and `-`, starting with a letter.

PER WORKLOAD. The infrastructure project `{customer_shortname}-deploy-<name>` under
`folder_workload_project_folder`, billed to the infrastructure billing account, with the
APIs of the entry's `apis`. Inside it the account `svc-deploy-<name>` and the state bucket
`{customer_shortname}-deploy-<name>-state`, which the account may write; the group reads
the project and may become the account — that account only. On the billing account the
account holds the entry's `billing_roles` (`roles/billing.user` unless the entry says
more), on the organisation `folder_workload_organization_roles` — `roles/browser` and
nothing else by default: an interface looks a folder up by its name among its parent's
folders, and that listing needs `resourcemanager.folders.list` on the parent.

PER FOLDER. The folder `<name>` (shown as `display_name` when the entry has one), and
`folder_workload_roles` for the workload's account on it: create and manage folders and
Google projects under it, set the IAM of its projects and enable their APIs. NOT granted:
access control on a folder, organisation policies, tags, billing administration — so an
account cannot grant itself anything on a folder, its own included, and reaches nothing
beside the folders it was given. A folder that already exists is declared as an entry and
taken over once with `satz adopt`, which finds it by its display name under its parent.

AN ENTRY THAT ASKS FOR MORE. `apis` and `billing_roles` are lists, and an entry that
states one states it whole: the six APIs below plus its own, `roles/billing.user` plus
its own.

WHAT A WORKLOAD'S ESTATE READS. Two interfaces, both taken to its `interfaces/incoming/` folder:
`workload-<name>` — `deploy_project_id` (its infrastructure project), `iac_account`, `state_bucket`, and what was
delegated to the account, `delegated_folder_roles`, `delegated_billing_roles`,
`delegated_apis`, which `satz` judges the estate's needs against — and `<folder name>`,
with `delegated_folder`, the parent of everything the estate creates. One estate reads
one folder's interface: a workload with two folders is rolled out by two estates that
run as the same account.

NO CLAIM. The workloads' identities are workloads, not controls: this pack witnesses nothing.

## Use it

```
params {
  use_folder_workload = true

  // the pack's own defaults — copy only the lines you change
  folder_workloads = []
  folder_workload_folders = []
  folder_workload_project_folder = ""
  folder_workload_roles = [
    "roles/resourcemanager.folderCreator",
    "roles/resourcemanager.folderEditor",
    "roles/resourcemanager.projectCreator",
    "roles/resourcemanager.projectDeleter",
    "roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin",
    "roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageAdmin",
  ]
  folder_workload_organization_roles = [ "roles/browser" ]
  folder_workload_group_roles = [
    "roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator",
    "roles/iam.serviceAccountUser",
  ]
}

use "presets/folder-workload.satz" when use_folder_workload
```

`use_folder_workload` is the gate: while it is falsy the pack contributes nothing — no resources, no params, no claims. It is declared by `estate_map`, and the estate's own binding wins.

**Needs from outside the pack:**

- `billing_account_infra` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `customer_shortname` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `default_region` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.

## Questions

What to ask before this pack is configured, and what changing the answer costs.

| asks about | prompt | reversal | blast | recommends |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `folder_workload_project_folder` | The folder the workloads' infrastructure projects are created in — the infrastructure folder as `google_folder.infra_folder.name`, another folder the estate declares as `google_folder.<label>.name`, an existing one by its numeric id, or empty for the organisation | edit | low | `"google_folder.infra_folder.name"` |

**folder_workload_project_folder** — It decides the policies the workloads' infrastructure projects inherit. Changing it afterwards moves every live one between parents.

An empty answer, `""`, is an answer: the organisation itself.

## Exports

Outputs of the root module and values of the interfaces under `interfaces/outgoing/` in every estate that uses this pack: a `core` export is carried by every interface, another one by its own interface and every interface that uses it. An interface a pack declares is common: every project's folder carries it.

| interface | output | value | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workload-{each.name}` | `deploy_project_id` | `"{customer_shortname}-deploy-{each.name}"` | The workload's infrastructure project: its plans are billed to it |
| `workload-{each.name}` | `iac_account` | `"svc-deploy-{each.name}@{customer_shortname}-deploy-{each.name}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"` | The service account the workload's estates run as |
| `workload-{each.name}` | `state_bucket` | `"{customer_shortname}-deploy-{each.name}-state"` | The bucket the workload's estates keep their states in |
| `workload-{each.name}` | `account_group` | `"{each.group}"` | The group whose members may act as the account |
| `workload-{each.name}` | `account_group_roles` | `folder_workload_group_roles` | What that group holds on the account |
| `workload-{each.name}` | `billing_account` | `billing_account_infra` | The billing account a new project is linked to |
| `workload-{each.name}` | `delegated_folder_roles` | `folder_workload_roles` | The roles the account holds on each of the workload's folders |
| `workload-{each.name}` | `delegated_billing_roles` | `each.billing_roles` | The roles the account holds on the billing account |
| `workload-{each.name}` | `delegated_apis` | `each.apis` | The APIs enabled on the workload's infrastructure project |
| `{each.name}` | `delegated_budgets` | `each.budgets` | Whether the account may manage budgets for the projects in this folder |
| `{each.name}` | `delegated_folder` | `"${google_folder.{each.name}.name}"` | The folder the workload's account works in: the parent of what its estate creates |

`workload-{each.name}` is written once per entry of `folder_workloads`, named by the entry's `name`, and each is one project's own interface, not a common one.

`{each.name}` is written once per entry of `folder_workload_folders`, named by the entry's `name`, and each is one project's own interface, not a common one.

## Requests

What a project may add to this pack's lists, through `contributes_<param>` in a file the estate uses after a reviewed pull request; `satz check-request` checks such a file.

| list | key | fields | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `folder_workloads` | `name` | `name` matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, `group` matching `[^@: ]+@[^@: ]+`, `apis`, `billing_roles` | A workload that rolls out folders and Google projects: its name, the address of the group that may become its account, the APIs of its infrastructure project and its roles on the billing account |
| `folder_workload_folders` | `name` | `name` matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, `workload` matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, `display_name`, `parent`, `budgets` | A folder a workload works in: the folder's name, the workload's name, the name the folder is shown under, and its parent |

_None — this pack proves no control by itself._

## History

| version | date | change |
|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | 2026-11-12 | a folder entry takes `budgets` (`false` when left out): `true` grants the workload's account the organisation's budget role on that folder, and so on the projects in it; the folder's interface publishes `delegated_budgets` |
| 2.0 | 2026-11-12 | the published values say `delegated_…` where they said `delivered_…`: `delegated_folder`, `delegated_folder_roles`, `delegated_billing_roles`, `delegated_apis`; the header calls the mechanism delegated access. Nothing the pack deploys changes |
| 1.2 | 2026-11-12 | the interface `workload-<name>` also publishes `account_group` and `account_group_roles` — who may act as the account — and `billing_account`, which a new project is linked to: the interface's README tells the team what it was handed and what to do with it |
| 1.1 | 2026-11-12 | the interface `workload-<name>` publishes the infrastructure project as `deploy_project_id`, where it said `project_id`: an estate that also reads a project's interface (`project-workload.satz`) reads `project_id` there |
| 1.0 | 2026-11-11 | first version, replacing `workload_deployer`: one identity per entry of `folder_workloads` (`{ name group apis billing_roles }` — infrastructure project, account, state bucket, the entry's APIs and billing roles) and one folder per entry of `folder_workload_folders` (`{ name workload display_name parent }`), created by the pack, with `folder_workload_roles` for the workload's account on that folder alone and no role that sets a folder's IAM; publishes the interfaces `workload-<name>` (identity and what was delivered) and `<folder>` (`delivered_folder`) |

The whole library's history: [the changelog](../CHANGELOG.md#changelog) in `presets/CHANGELOG.md`.
